SUBJECT:  Zilo International Group LLC Contract Award

RECOMMENDED ACTION(S): Authorize the City Manager to execute a contract with Zilo
International Group LLC for a not-to-exceed sum of $35,000.

REPORT SUMMARY: The City of Avalon actively pursues state and federal grant opportunities
to assist with City identified unfunded projects and programs. Many funding agencies utilize US
Census income data to determine grant eligibility and funding reimbursement levels.

The current City of Avalon Median Household Income (MHI), per the 2021 US Census American
Community Survey 5-Year Estimates, is $77644 (+1- $18,531). Staff believes this does not
accurately capture the City of Avalon’s true MHI. In order to resolve this discrepancy, City Staff
are recommending completing a Community Wide Survey.

On April 5, 2023, City staff issued a Request for Proposal for professional services to conduct a
Community Wide Survey for the City of Avalon. Despite advertising for the services, only one
proposal, from Zilo International Group LLC, was received. City staff reviewed the proposal and
received a presentation, concluding Zilo International Group LLC is well-qualified. The firm has
experience working with cities and other public agencies in completing a wide variety of surveys,
including community surveys. Therefore, it is recommended to award a contract to Zilo
International Group LLC.

FISCAL IMPACTS: The survey has been budgeted in the FY2023/24 General Fund Operating
Budget and will assist City Staff with a broader range of grant opportunities.

GOAL ALIGNMENT: Grant Funding Opportunities

CONSEQUENCES OF NOT FOLLOWING RECOMMENDED ACTION: Future grant funding
eligibility and reimbursement levels will be based on the 2021 US Census American Community
Survey data.

FOLLOW UP ACTION: Execute a professional services agreement with Zilo Associates.
Develop a stakeholder community group to assist with the survey implementation and return to
City Council to publish the final report in approximately five months.

ADVERTISING, NOTICE AND PUBLIC CONTACT: The item was properly listed on the posted
agenda pursuant to the Brown Act.

SUBJECT:  Award Above Ground Fuel Tank Procurement

RECOMMENDED ACTION(S): Authorize the City Manager or his designee to procure an above
ground fuel tank from Western Pump per the specifications designated for the Underground Fuel
Tank Replacement Project at a cost not to exceed $160,000.

REPORT SUMMARY: The State of California requires the owners or operators of specific types
of underground fuel storage tanks to permanently close by December 31, 2025. The City of
Avalon owns four underground fuel tanks at the Avalon Fuel Dock that fall under this
requirement.

With assistance from former Assemblymember Patrick O’Donnell, the City was awarded a
$500,000 State budget earmark that is administered through the State of California Water Board
to remove the underground fuel tanks located at the fuel dock and install an above ground
system in compliance with the new regulations. The granting agreement requires the City to
complete the project by November 30, 2023.

The project is included in the FY22-23 Budget and Capital Improvement Plan  —  Project Number
207004, Account Number 11470-6547 with $700,000 budgeted.
  —

On March 21, 2023 City Council approved the design and construction documents for this
project, and authorized Staff to post and receive informal bids to procure the fuel tank for an
amount not to exceed $200,000. Two bids were received and opened June 16, 2023 that fulfilled
the bid requirements. Western Pump presented the lowest bid of $137,283.30. A second bid
was received from CJW Construction Inc. for $259,000. Staff is recommending authorization to
procure the fuel tank from Western Pump as they fulfilled the bid requirement at the lowest price.
A not to exceed request of a $160,000 includes a contingency for any unforeseen changes or
costs as the procurement is finalized.

This is one of three contracts anticipated to procure the resources to complete this project at the
most competitive cost. In addition to this procurement there will be a construction contract for
the above ground tank enclosure and another construction contract to provide the gas station
scope of work as well as removing the underground tanks.

GOAL ALIGNMENT: City Infrastructure. Reduction of high-risk facilities.

FISCAL IMPACTS: Total expenditure is not to exceed $160,000 towards CIP project code
207004 (account 11470-6547).
 CONSEQUENCES OF NOT FOLLOWING RECOMMENDED ACTION: The City may not meet
the timeline required by the funding agreement with the State of California Water Board.

FOLLOW UP ACTION: Procure above ground fuel tank from Western Pump.

RECOMMENDED ACTION(S): (1) Adjust the Fiscal Year 2022-2023 Budget to reassign
$305,500 from Commuter Subsidy Program (12230-5099) to Vehicle Replacement (12230-
6781). (2) Authorize the City Manager or his designee to purchase five (5) E6 GEM LSV
Vehicles, two (2) digital sign boards and other items to install charging infrastructure and assist
with emergency response for a not to exceed sum of $305,500.

REPORT SUMMARY: The City of Avalon annually applies for Proposition A Incentive Funds
through the Los Angeles County Metropolitan Transportation Authority (Metro). The City has
received $1,000,000 in Proposition A Incentive Funds annually over the last several fiscal years,
with $700,000 earmarked for the commuter subsidy program, and $300,000 earmarked for the
City’s land transit system. In addition to these annual funds, the City received an additional
$586,412 in ARPA Act equivalent Program Funds in the current fiscal year through the
Proposition A Incentive Program to support transit programs impacted by the COVID-19
pandemic. The City received a signed Memorandum of Understanding authorizing the award of
these funds in November 2022. These funds must be spent in the current fiscal year for the
City’s commuter or and transit programs.

At the May 16, 2023 City Council Meeting, City Staff recommended allocating the ARPA Act
equivalent funds between both transit programs, with $286,412 to increased commuter subsidy
and $300,000 for land transit improvements. At the meeting, the City Council approved the use
of the $286,412 in ARPA Act equivalent funds to provide an additional one-time $85 increase in
the commuter book subsidy for the month of June 2023. The purpose of the increased subsidy
was to offset the impact of pandemic-related inflation on cross channel ferry commuting costs
for residents.

The City’s fixed route transit ridership dropped dramatically as a result of the pandemic and has
not fully recovered, with current year farebox revenues down 16.1% compared to 2019. Public
transit agencies across the state have experienced similar downturns in ridership. City Staff
recommends utilizing the ARPA Act equivalent funds to respond to changes in consumer
demands and make improvements to its fixed route fleet by transitioning to smaller, open air,
electric vehicles to provide better ventilation and reduced crowding.
 In studying transit trends throughout Southern California and considering the findings from the
Mode Shift Study completed in 2023, Staff determined the development of a microtransit system
would be the best fit for the community. Not only will the vehicle fleet have a significantly smaller
footprint reducing traffic and congestion the smaller, open-air vehicle will provide for a better
  —  —

overall experience for the rider.

City Staff researched microtransit systems currently in operation in other cities, including
Anaheim, Long Beach, and San Diego. All three cities utilize Polaris GEM E6 vehicles to facilitate
a point-to-point on demand transit system.

The Polaris GEM E6 provides a versatile and durable vehicle with proven success in providing
high volume, mass transportation in other Southern California cities. Manufactured in Anaheim,
California, the vehicles are electric with zero emissions and exceed Low Speed Vehicle federal
manufacturing standards.

SUBJECT:  Award 206 F. Whittley Housing Project

RECOMMENDED ACTION(S): (1) Review the bid results. (2) Award a construction contract if
an acceptable bid is received, or reject all bids(3) If bids are rejected, adopt a Resolution
Pursuant to Public Contracts Code 201767 by 4 /5 vote Authorizing the City Manager or his
designee to negotiate the construction contract for the 206 F. Whittley Housing and Site
Preparation project.

REPORT SUMMARY: A multi-family property at 206 E. Whittley was purchased by the ACIA in
2008 with the intent to provide affordable housing units. In July 2019, the City Council, acting
as the Housing Authority, approved final construction plans to renovate the structure and
authorized Staff to develop and release a request for proposals to rehabilitate the property to be
rented to low- and moderate-income residents. That project has been delayed due to impacts
from the pandemic but is scheduled to be released for bidding in early summer.

In October 2019, the City Council acting as Housing Authority authorized City Staff to develop a
site plan and feasibility study for the development of five additional units through the replacement
of a stand-alone single unit structure located on the southeastern portion of the property. Due to
water allocations not being available for a period of time and Staff/financial reductions due to the
pandemic, work was put on hold for the development of the second building. Once water
allocations became a possibility, a renewed effort was put forward to gain a water allocation.
The concept was submitted to Southern California Edison and a water allocation was received.
The water allocation requires that timely progress be made towards the completion of the project.

In preparation for these projects a joint effort by City Staff and local contractors recently
completed improvements to the sewer lateral and water lines from East Whittley to the property.
As a result of this effort all utilities are onsite and at the needed capacity for the existing and the
proposed additional building.

In developing the plan for the second building, geotechnical engineers determined the existing
retaining walls at the property’s boundaries need remediation to extend their service life in the
case of the existing building or replacement in the case of the new building, due to corrosion on
the existing tiebacks and age of the concrete.

In order to ensure the opportunity for highest and best use of the property, Staff proposes
remediation of the existing retaining wall, and additionally leveling and backfilling of an adjacent
area that will widen and recapture areas of the southern portion of the East Whittley public right
of-way at the 90-degree curve. The elevation and further frontage improvements of the right-of-
 way will allow for on-site parking for all nine (9) future housing units (four in the original building
and up to five in the new structure) and also provide three additional public parking spaces on
East Whittley. The proposal will repurpose the existing on-street parking area and provide a
convenient stopping/loading/unloading area for large delivery or trash vehicles in the roadway,
as well as provide better emergency access/staging. While this widening will reduce one
informal unmaintained access to the back of the Hermosa Hotel, the primary access point at the
 Museum’ public stairway will continue to provide a safe direct connection to the upper rear
walkway of the Hermosa complex. This access point will be further improved with the project.

City Council acting as Housing Authority approved the design and construction documents,
along with the release of a Request for Proposal May 2, 2023.

Due to the complexity of the project and the formal bid requirements the project bid opening was
extended until June 27, 2023.

Staff recommends the City Council acting as Housing Authority review the bids and determine if
an acceptable bid was received. If an acceptable bid is not received, City Staff recommend
rejecting all bids and adopting a resolution authorizing the City Manager or his designee to
negotiate the construction contract for the 206 E. Whittley Housing project.

will not be able to utilize the entire parcel at its highest and best use. The expenditure of these
funds will directly impact the availability of affordable housing.

FOLLOW UP ACTION: Implement Housing Authority direction.
